audience.programmeDescription: Cybersecurity & Cybercrime at Leiden combines computing, governance, law and criminology to study digital security and crime. Students examine how networked systems work, how attacks occur, who commits and experiences cybercrime, and how organisations and public institutions can respond. Research methods, academic skills and multidisciplinary projects connect these perspectives.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete UCR comparison is not yet available because the compulsory third-year curriculum has not been fully established from the available official information. The supported first two years and elective space are shown below. This uncertainty does not establish that UCR offers no suitable study possibilities.

curriculum.limitation: The listed components total 150 EC: 120 EC of compulsory study in the first two years and 30 EC of third-year elective space. The remaining 30 EC of compulsory third-year study, including the final project, still require confirmation. This is an incomplete curriculum, not a certified 180-EC degree plan.

componentNotes.y1-skills-1: The skills labs develop academic and professional skills in small groups. Attendance and assessment requirements apply.
componentNotes.y1-project: A 10-EC multidisciplinary project on online deception and disinformation. Its credits are counted once within the first year.
componentNotes.y2-defence: Builds on the study of cyber attacks, moving from vulnerabilities to access controls, defensive measures and organisational security.
componentNotes.y2-project: A 10-EC multidisciplinary ransomware project, counted within the second year. Attendance and individual assessment requirements apply.
componentNotes.y3-open-elective-space: 30 EC for electives, a minor or approved study or internship options. Level, approval and non-overlap rules apply. Honours courses and specified overlapping minors and courses cannot be used here.
